name: Generate a recurring report
definition: Enable a requester to receive a report, produced on a schedule or on demand, that reflects current data against stated parameters -- without requiring a suitable report-generation implementation to already exist before the first request.
capabilityPurpose: Enable a defined report to be produced repeatedly from current data, without the requester having to build or maintain the generation logic themselves.

includes: Specifying the report's parameters and cadence
Producing one report instance per request or scheduled occurrence
When no suitable generation implementation yet exists, constructing and validating one as part of fulfilling that occurrence
excludes: Authoring or approving the report's underlying business definition/template
Distributing the produced report to its recipients
Modifying the underlying source data being reported on

meaningfulOutcome: A report instance is produced that reflects the current data against the stated parameters, or the attempt is rejected or deferred with an identifiable reason.

interactionContracts.name: Request a recurring report
interactionContracts.commandIntent: Define report parameters and a production cadence (on demand, or on a schedule)
interactionContracts.currentState: No report definition exists for this request

policiesInvariants.text: Parameters must be sufficient to determine what data the report draws on and how it is scoped.

interactionContracts.transition: No report definition to a standing report definition
interactionContracts.result: Report definition acknowledged and scheduled (or ready for on-demand production)

interactionContracts.name: Produce report
interactionContracts.actor: An agent (while constructing and running a new implementation), or a previously agent-built implementation (running unattended, or reused under an agent's direct supervision)
interactionContracts.commandIntent: Produce one report instance matching the current definition against current data
interactionContracts.currentState: A standing report definition exists; this occurrence is due (by schedule or on-demand request)

policiesInvariants.text: A produced report instance must reflect the actual current data available at generation time -- it must not silently substitute stale or cached data without disclosing that it did.

interactionContracts.transition: Due occurrence to produced report instance, or an identifiable failure
interactionContracts.result: A report instance, or an identifiable failure reason (e.g. data unavailable, parameters no longer resolvable)
unknowns: Where a constructed implementation is stored, versioned, and audited
Policy for retiring an implementation once report parameters change materially

rulesInvariants.text: An agent-built implementation must be validated against the current report parameters before it is reused, unattended, for a subsequent occurrence.

recommendedDefaults.text: If a previously agent-built implementation fails validation against new parameters or a changed data shape, fall back to agent-primary construction again for that occurrence rather than silently reusing an implementation that no longer fits.

unknowns: Where a constructed implementation is stored, versioned, and audited
Policy for retiring an implementation once report parameters change materially
How a partial or degraded data source is disclosed within a produced report

realizations.name: Agent constructs, then produces, the first occurrence
realizations.rationaleIntent: The first time this report definition is due, no suitable generation implementation exists yet. An agent interprets the parameters, determines that no reusable implementation is available, builds a function or script that produces the report from the current data, and validates it before producing this occurrence's report instance with it.

implementationRequirements.text: The newly built implementation must pass validation against the current parameters (and a known-correct sample, if one is available) before it is treated as reusable for future occurrences.

realizations.name: Agent-built implementation produces subsequent occurrences
realizations.rationaleIntent: Once Realization A's implementation has been validated, every subsequent due occurrence of Produce report runs that implementation directly and deterministically -- the same Interaction Contract MLE and required outcome, now served by construction provenance (agent-built-software) paired with an ordinary, agent-uninvolved execution mode (software-primary).

realizations.name: Agent-built implementation is reused under direct agent supervision
realizations.rationaleIntent: Report parameters changed since Realization A's implementation was last validated. Rather than trust it to run unattended (Realization B) or discard it and start over, an agent reuses the same agent-built implementation but directly invokes and supervises this occurrence's run, checking its output against the changed parameters before the implementation earns unattended (Realization B) status again. Construction provenance is unchanged from Realization B; only who controls this occurrence's execution differs -- this is the evidence that agent-built-software does not force software-primary execution.

implementationRequirements.text: The supervising agent must confirm the agent-built implementation's output against the current parameters before either releasing this occurrence's report or restoring the implementation to unattended (Realization B) use.

agenticMappings.notes: Realization A only -- invoked when no valid implementation currently exists for this report definition.
Supports Request a recurring report and validation in Produce report.
Supports Produce report in all three realizations.

Realizations B and C -- the artifact Realization A constructed and validated; not a skill in either realization, since no agent reasoning occurs inside the implementation itself, only around it in Realization C.

provenance.text: This is an illustrative example, not extracted from a real reporting system. It exists to make explicit that agent-built-software is implementation provenance, while execution mode is a separate, runtime-control question (specification section 3.3), demonstrated across three realizations rather than two so that provenance and execution mode are shown moving independently, not merely differing once: Realizations B and C share kind (agent-built-software) with different execution modes, and Realization A shares neither kind nor execution mode with B or C.
